subject: Post-demo: deployment fit & hosted evaluation checklist
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@cloudmetrics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: deployment fit & hosted evaluation checklist

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciated the thoughtful questions. I pulled together a short recap and a few asks so we can size the right evaluation path (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and get you onto a pilot quickly.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary goal: add a semantic search + chat assistant inside CloudMetrics for customer support workflows.
- Data sensitivity: some incoming content may include customer PII; you need audit logs and log-redaction controls.
- Traffic: expected baseline ~50 r/s with spikes to ~200 r/s during reports refresh; typical prompt length ~150 tokens, responses ~80 tokens.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 250ms for single-turn generative calls.

Immediate asks (to pick a deployment mode)
1) Can you confirm whether the data passed to the model will include regulated PII that must stay within your VPC (yes/no)? If yes, we should scope Private deployment or Dedicated with a VPC peering option.
2) Please complete the attached traffic_profile_template.xlsx with typical QPS, burst length (seconds), and concurrency per worker.
3) Are you comfortable starting on Hosted API for the pilot if we provide a reserved-throughput sandbox with tighter rate limits and audit logs?

What Hosted covers for the pilot (quick wins)
- Dedicated sandbox throughput: we can reserve a pair of workers with predictable throughput for pilot traffic.
- Token-level cost visibility and per-route latency breakdowns.
- Streaming endpoints and function-calling support for conversational flows.
- Audit logs, request/response redaction options, and RBAC controls.

Attachments included: rwd_quickstart_checklist.pdf (pilot steps & sample curl), traffic_profile_template.xlsx (please fill).

Next steps
- Jordan: send the completed traffic template and confirm PII requirement.
- Aditya: I’ll loop you in to prepare an initial Hosted sandbox config and rough cost estimate.
- Once we have the template, we’ll propose either: (A) Hosted sandbox pilot with guarded rate limits and logging, or (B) a Dedicated capacity estimate if you need VPC-only data paths.

Thanks — happy to jump back on a 30-min call if helpful.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@cloudmetrics.com>

Date: 2026-10-05T18:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment fit & hosted evaluation checklist

Thanks — this is great, Hannah. Quick clarifications:

1) PII scope: most of the content is customer emails and ticket text; we consider email addresses and account IDs as sensitive. We can redact some fields but not all. Our security team will want to know if Hosted can support strict log-redaction and whether logs can be excluded entirely.

2) Traffic template: will fill and return today. Two more data points: expected monthly token volume ~120M tokens, and peak bursts usually last 45–90s.

3) Rate limits: what are the default rate caps on Hosted for the streaming endpoint (/v1/stream) and for concurrent requests? Also, if we push through batching on our side, how does that map to token billing and latency?

4) If we start Hosted and later move to Dedicated or Private, how smooth is model pinning/version continuity? We don’t want tokenization or model differences to cause regressions.

If you can answer 1,3,4 I’ll prioritize the template.

—Jordan
Jordan Lee
Head of Platform Engineering | CloudMetrics
jordan.lee@cloudmetrics.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@cloudmetrics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T21:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment fit & hosted evaluation checklist

Jordan — answers inline below. Appreciate the token estimate and burst note.

1) Hosted & PII/logs
- Hosted can be configured to redact or drop request/response payloads from audit logs for specific routes; we also support disabling payload retention entirely for enterprise customers. For your security team we recommend Hosted + VPC peering + a strict retention policy for the pilot; if they still require all traffic to never leave your VPC, we’ll scope Private.

3) Rate limits & billing
- Default Hosted sandbox limits: 60 concurrent requests and a soft QPS cap tied to token rate (roughly 300 tokens/sec per worker by default). For pilots we typically provision a reserved sandbox with explicit caps (e.g., 250 r/s aggregate).
- Streaming endpoint (/v1/stream): streaming calls count against concurrency and token throughput; long-lived streams are best when you need partial outputs — they still bill per-token consumed.
- Batching: server-side batching reduces per-token compute cost and can improve p95 latency for high-throughput workloads. From a billing perspective, tokens are charged per model compute, independent of whether you batch, but batching improves throughput and can lower unit cost.

4) Model continuity (Hosted -> Dedicated/Private)
- We support model pinning and release channels. We can pin an exact model artifact (same weights + tokenizer config) so you won’t see divergence when moving environments. Ops teams typically run a short A/B validation on a held-out eval set during cutover; we’ll help automate that as part of the migration playbook.

Attachments: I attached the quickstart checklist and the blank traffic template again. Filling the template will let us size the sandbox and propose either: Hosted reserved sandbox (fast path) or Dedicated capacity estimate with VPC-only networking (if your security team requires it).

If you want me to loop in a solutions engineer for a technical review of redaction/retention, say the word and I’ll add them.

Best,
Hannah

Attachments: rwd_quickstart_checklist.pdf, traffic_profile_template.xlsx

Marissa — forwarding the thread with CloudMetrics (deal RID-4732). They’re open to Hosted pilot but security may push for Dedicated/Private depending on our redaction guarantees. Can you draft: (A) a Hosted sandbox quote for a 60–90 day pilot with a 250 r/s reserved cap and audit-log redaction enabled, and (B) a rough Dedicated capacity estimate with VPC peering and monthly commit tiers (50K / 100K token commit examples) so we can show both paths?

Key props: monthly ~120M tokens (they reported), peak bursts 45–90s at ~200 r/s, latency p95 target 250ms. Please include an ops handoff meeting line item for a validation run (A/B eval) during migration.

Thanks — cc’ing Aditya so he can prepare the sandbox config once we sign.

Hannah
